title: Evolutionary Characterization of Leaf Rust Resistance Genes in Wheat Triticum aestivum ssp. and T. monococcum
content: The leaf rust resistance genes provides partial but consistent and stable resistance across multiple seasons and periods. In this study, evolutionary relationships between these genes were analyzed by constructing a phylogenetic tree using the neighbor-joining and motif analysis with its graphical representation via the ClustalW algorithm and R. showing one motif across G3 to G11 at the same position implied functional similarity or shared regulatory role or evolutionary constraint. A high significant motif was observed in Gen1 and Gen2 indicated an important active sites. In addition, these genes was divided into two main groups using phylogenetic tree. The first node was from Gen1 to Gen10, reflected strong evidence of being monophyletic, while the intermediate nodes from Gen13 to Gen18 reflected very weak evidence to determine the detailed ancestor relationships. The active sites that must remain functionally constant ranged from 107 to 301 using sequences logo, which shows forceful conservation at some positions at P, L, P, R, F, L, G, L, L, and K while, from 200 to 260 was not conserved. The sequences of these genes aimed to perform an evolutionary and molecular characterization based on wheat (Triticum aestivum ssp) genome. Collectively, these findings determine a valuable establishment for future molecular breeding strategies.
